issues.where: fit_sh / res['shN'] = sh[:,1:] with DC replaced by RGB2SH(reference colour)
issues.problem: The pinv solution Y+ (O-0.5) is minimum-norm over all 16 coefficients, so it spreads the mean colour over the higher-order bands in proportion to Y_m (DC basis 0.282 is small). Keeping only H[1:] and then overwriting DC with the full reference colour double counts the colour: once SH degree >=1 switches on (step 1000), the Gaussian's colour at the reference view jumps by |Y_rest.H_rest|, not 0. Garden sidecar: median per-point max|shN| = 0.16, p99 = 1.69, 0.69% > 2, max 217. In a synthetic reproduction (two views 0.5-15 deg apart, near-equal colours, DC replaced) the rendered reference colour differs from the observation by a median of 0.22 (p99 0.32) at degree 3. The paper (Sec 3.5 / supp.) says 'initialize all coefficients except index 0 using Y+O' but not how DC and rest are made consistent, and gives no clamp or regulariser.
issues.evidence: paper supp. 'Spherical harmonics initialization' (pseudoinverse for all but index 0; DC from reference pixel) vs core.fit_sh + preprocess.py:~150 (res['shN']=sh[:,1:]). Probe sh_fit only checks (a) Y.H reproduces both observations BEFORE DC replacement and (b) degree-0 render equals ref colour; the composed (replaced-DC) init is never checked.
issues.fix: Make the composed init self-consistent while still pinv-based: set DC = RGB2SH(ref colour), then solve the rest on the residual, H_rest = pinv(Y[:,1:]) (O - 0.5 - Y0*H0), so degree-3 render at the reference direction equals the reference colour (and the neighbour view is reproduced). Report both variants (literal-paper and residual) in the benchmark beside edgs-nosh, and add a probe asserting the composed render at the reference direction equals the reference colour. If the literal variant is kept, state clearly that it is a reading of an ambiguous paper and that results may be worse than edgs-nosh.

issues.problem: No handling of near-parallel view pairs: pinv of nearly collinear rows yields coefficients up to 217 (0.7% > 2). The paper has no principled clamp, so any clamp (e.g. |H| <= some value) would be a new, undocumented hyper-parameter; but leaving the values unbounded risks exploding view-dependent colour that the optimizer (shN lr 1.25e-4) cannot repair. The residual formulation above (or Tikhonov/rcond truncation of pinv) is the principled alternative; a hard clamp should only be a documented deviation.
issues.fix: Use pinv with an rcond/ridge (document), or the residual fit; if clamping, log it as a deviation and run edgs vs edgs-nosh to bound it.

Official maps RoMa's normalized coords with (W-1)/2 (align_corners=True) and also feeds them to the 3DGS projection; plugin uses pixel-centre (2i+1)/W-1 consistently with the 3DGS rasterizer. fidelity_gaps_confirmed: Training-split-only init CONFIRMED: preprocess.initialize_scene uses dataset['splits']['train'] (load_dataset, llffhold8) for frames, viewmats, k-means reference views, nearest neighbours, RoMa pairs, SH observations and colours; garden edgs_init.json: 161 train views, 161 reference views subset of train, 0 of the 24 held-out (sorted[::8]) names present; no test image touches points/scales/opacities/SH. Runtime camera-extent hook also receives train cameras only.

Matching/geometry settings match the official code: RoMa outdoors, upsample_preds=False, symmetric=False, k-means on flattened W2C, 3 NN by Frobenius W2C distance (self excluded), max-aggregated confidence, multinomial w/o replacement, M=25000 (garden 4,025,000 sampled / 4,024,822 kept after tau_proj 0.01), scale=0.001*0.5*dist isotropic, opacity logit 0 (0.5), identity quats.

Density schedule matches trainer.py: prune opacity<0.005 every step while step<15000 (1-based), opacity logit += log 0.99 every 10 steps while <15000 (official log(exp(x)*0.99)), no densify/reset, opacity LR 0.025, means LR lr(max(step,8000)) applied for the next step; lr_floored equals 3DGS log-linear schedule.

--recipe splatstudio workaround is sound: runtime differences vs 3dgs are only (a) scene_scale = 0.9-quantile of points instead of 1.1*max camera-centre spread and (b) the 3-NN log-scale init; (b) is overwritten by the sidecar in density.initialize and (a) is undone in set_training_cameras (base_lr/runtime_scene_scale*camera_extent, training cameras only, same 1.1*max-dist as getNerfppNorm, floor 0.01 both sides); the runtime's own per-step LR reset is overridden each step by after_backward. Other LRs (scales .005, quats .001, sh0 .0025, shN .0025/20, opacity set to .025) are scale-independent. Result equals the official setup apart from documented gaps (white bg, sampling).

SHA-256 link verified: garden points.npz sha256 == edgs_init.npz points_sha256 == edgs_init.json points_sha256; runtime hash is over float32 means in original order (valid because num_gaussians >= N so no subsample); lookup fails loudly otherwise.

summary: Leakage check passes: only training views are used everywhere in preprocessing (verified in code and garden edgs_init.json). RoMa matching, DLT triangulation, thresholds, scales/opacities, no-densify schedule, LR hold, SHA link and the splatstudio recipe workaround all match the official code. Not approved because of the reconstructed SH initialization: dropping H[0] from a min-norm 16-coefficient pinv and replacing DC double counts the colour (median reference-view colour shift ~0.2 once SH bands activate), outliers up to 217 are unhandled, and the sh-fit probe cannot see it. edgs-nosh is unaffected and is the safer headline variant until this is fixed. Minor: stale --recipe 3dgs in README/plan, missing T&T/DB #G and time in paper_results.json.
